Done. I diagnosed the problem class and produced a verified, self-contained solution.

## Deliverables

- **`~/solution.md`** — the full solution document (title, root-cause analysis, exact fix with code, verification).
- **`~/mvcc/`** — the runnable reference implementation:
  - `mvcc.go` (554 lines) — snapshot-isolated MVCC store + serialization-graph conflict detection
  - `mvcc_test.go` (271 lines) — reproduction + regression tests
  - `go.mod`

## Root causes identified

1. **Phantom blindness** — `Scan` recorded only the keys materialized at snapshot time. A concurrent insert into the interval produced no `rw` anti-dependency, so range write skew committed.
2. **Watermark starvation** — read-only snapshots were never released, pinning the GC low-water mark; the naive "fix" aborts long readers instead. The correct fix is to **promote** a cycle-free read-only transaction out of the active set, then GC.
3. **Abort cascades** — aborting on predicate *overlap* rather than on a real **cycle** in the serialization graph. Disjoint workloads were being aborted together.

## The fix

- Store the predicate `[lo, hi)` on every `Scan` and test candidate writes by interval containment.
- On commit, materialize `rw`/`wr`/`ww` edges against all active/committed peers and abort **iff** the committing node can reach itself (`reachesLocked(id, id)`).
- Compute the watermark as the oldest active snapshot; keep the newest version at/below it plus all newer versions; drop committed metadata/deps below it.
- Read-only transactions participate in cycle detection at commit, then release their snapshot (serialized-transaction promotion).

## Verification (`go test -race -count=1 -v ./...`, Go 1.26.8)

All 9 tests pass, `gofmt`/`go vet` clean, race-free. Highlights:
- write skew and range phantoms → exactly one abort, invariant preserved;
- the buggy point-only scan is reproduced as a passing test documenting the anomaly;
- disjoint ranges / 16 independent keys → **0** aborts (no cascade);
- long reader: watermark advances from `reader.StartTS()` to `Seq()` and versions drop 3→1 **without aborting the reader**;
- 8×200 concurrent read-modify-writes → thousands of conflicts, `counter == 1600` (no lost update).

signatures.description: Build a key-value store with snapshot isolation over an append-only MVCC version chain, where range queries must detect phantoms (writes that would have changed a previously-read range). Implement SSI-style conflict detection with read-range watermarks and serialized-transaction promotion, deciding abort vs. commit when two concurrent transactions each take range locks on overlapping predicates. The hard part is watermark advance without starving long-running readers and avoiding false-positive abort cascades under write-skew workloads.
